'''Peter Jagers''' (12th March 1941) is a professor emeritus of mathematical statistics at [[University of Gothenburg]] and [[Chalmers University of Technology]] who made lasting contributions in [[probability]] and [[Branching process|general branching processes]].<ref name=":0" /> Jagers was first vice president (2007–2010) of [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences|the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Nerman|first=Olle|date=1 February 2019|title=Peter Jagers: a collegial perspective|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/advances-in-applied-probability/article/peter-jagers-a-collegial-perspective/E6EC166CFF4DD9723CF80AB1FB5DE38C|journal=Advances in Applied Probability|volume=50A|pages=3–9|via=Applied Probability Trust}}</ref> and chair of the [[Royal Society of Arts and Sciences in Gothenburg]] (2012).<ref name=":0" /> He in an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Individual - ISI|url=https://www.isi-web.org/about-isi/who-is-isi/members/indivual|access-date=30 July 2021|website=Individual Members|archive-date=5 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211005043450/https://www.isi-web.org/about-isi/who-is-isi/members/indivual|url-status=dead}}</ref> a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honored IMS Fellows|url=https://imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/|access-date=July 29, 2021}}</ref> and past president of the [[Bernoulli Society]] (2005–2007).<ref>{{Cite web|title=About the Bernoulli Society: History|url=http://www.bernoulli-society.org/about-the-bs#History|access-date=31 July 2021|website=Bernoulli Society|archive-date=28 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928081804/http://www.bernoulli-society.org/about-the-bs#History|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also served as a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of [[Statistics Sweden]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Förteckning över ämnen|url=https://www.scb.se/contentassets/0e274f9c94be42f684a85917508671fd/forteckning-over-amnen-behandlade-av-scbs_vetenskapliga_rad.pdf|website=List of topics discussed by the SCB Scientific Advisory Board (in Swedish)}}</ref>

Jagers has been coordinating editor of the ''[[Journal of Applied Probability]]'' and ''[[Advances in Applied Probability]]''. He is on the editorial committee for [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]]'s books on probability theory<ref>{{Cite web|title=Probability Theory and Stochastic Modelling|url=https://www.springer.com/series/13205?detailsPage=aboutTheEditor|access-date=July 29, 2021|website=About the editor}}</ref> and was editor of [[Stochastic Processes and Their Applications|Stochastic Processes and their Applications]] 1989–1993.<ref name=":0" />

== Honors and awards ==
Jagers received an honorary doctorate from the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0" /> and in 2012 was awarded the Carver Medal by the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=August 2012|title=Peter Jagers selected to receive 2012 IMS Carver award|url=https://imstat.org/wp-content/uploads/Bulletin41_5.pdf|journal=IMS Bulletin|volume=41|pages=2|via=IMS}}</ref> In 2003 he received the Chalmers Medal<ref>{{Cite web|date=2 March 2021|title=Peter Jagers|url=https://www.chalmers.se/sv/om-chalmers/akademiska-hogtider/promotion/chalmersmedaljen/Sidor/peter-jagers.aspx|access-date=30 July 2021|website=About Chalmers}}</ref> and in 2005 was awarded King [[Carl XVI Gustaf]] 's gold medal for "services to mathematics in Sweden and internationally".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sök ordens- och medaljförläningar (in Swedish)|url=https://www.kungahuset.se/monarkinhovstaterna/ordnarochmedaljer/medaljer/medaljer/sokmedalj.4.30963a1811be3fda3ab800012080.html?medaljar=2005&medaljtyp=0&medaljnamn=Peter+Jagers|website=Sök-Medalj-Sveriges Kungahus}}</ref>

== Publications ==
He has published a large number of scientific works, notably in [[branching process]] theory and its applications, and is the author of two books, Branching Processes with Biological Applications (J. Wiley 1975) and Branching Processes: Variation, Growth, and Extinction of Populations (Cambridge U. Press 2005). The Crump-Mode-Jagers (or generalized) branching process is named for Jagers.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Trayanov|first=Plamen|title=Branching Processes and Their Applications|publisher=Springer|year=2016|isbn=978-3-319-31639-0|pages=167–182}}</ref>
